name: Build a loose future-garage/ambient drum groove in layers: halftime kick and rim, a guide 'base hat' on every 'and', accent hats and rims on hand-swung 16ths (some early, some late, some on the grid), flair hats from one sample with a reversed copy, then faded Foley chops for crunch. Process it with LP24 on the kick (about 1 kHz, 30% resonance) and a band-passed rim (about 1.5 kHz), a frequency shift on the hat group (example -898 Hz), the rims vocoding themselves with chorus, a fast unsynced auto-pan and phaser on Foley (about 6.1 Hz), a half-note volume duck on the hat group, and a 12-bit lo-fi sampler with gentle clip/saturation on the drum bus
goal: A restrained, organic, swinging drum groove that sits behind ambient pads (lo-fi, in the background, not in-your-face like dubstep/D&B), varied every 2-4 bars so it doesn't sound loopy.

source.title: Future garage / ambient drum patterns, layer by layer, plus post-processing

prerequisites: Kick, rim shot, several hat samples, home Foley recordings (silverware, paper, celery) chopped to single clicks
Filter with saturation, frequency shifter, a vocoder with self-carrier mode and chorus, auto-pan, phaser, volume LFO shaper, bit-crusher/sampler emulator, soft and hard clipper

inputs.name: feel
inputs.description: halftime (two-step in half time) or fulltime (snare on 2 and near 4)

outputs.name: drum_layers
outputs.description: Kick/rim, base hat, accent hats/rims, flair hats, Foley layers

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Fits Matt's taste: bring the kick and rim in early; the groove is quiet and restrained enough to run under an intro pad.
The frequency shift is a static offset on the drum groups (no LFO on shift amount), so pitch stays steady. Swing and timing looseness are timing only, not pitch.
Use different but similar samples for repeated Foley hits, since one sample every time sounds repetitive.
Portable to Polyrhythm Studio as layered step patterns with per-step micro-timing offsets and per-group filter/bitcrush.
Auto-generated YouTube Show transcript; values are as spoken and approximate where the speaker says 'about' or 'around'.

steps.action: Core: kick plus main rim in a halftime two-step (one-drop/dub feel), or fulltime with the snare on 2 and near 4.
Add a guide 'base hat' on the 'and' of every beat to feel out the spaces. It may be muted in the final mix.

Add 2-3 accent-hat layers on other 16ths/8ths. Swing the 2nd and 4th 16ths by hand and not precisely: some hits on the grid, some a little late, some early, until it feels right. Do the same with accent rims for mid-range knock. Group and duplicate the loop, then vary it every 2-4 bars (move hits, swap a sound, stop a layer briefly, a small filter sweep).
Make flair hats from one hat sample with velocity changes for bounce, plus a reversed copy placed every so often.

Foley crunch: chop a recording (silverware, paper) into single clicks. Line the transients up roughly with a grid value just before the main rim, or on a swung 16th. Fade each chop in and out to soften the transients. Add a transient-heavy 'mid knock' layer (example: celery snaps).

Filter the kick with LP24 at 30% resonance and the cutoff around 1 kHz (range 800 Hz-3 kHz depending on the kick). Put the rim through a band-pass/high-pass blend at about 1.5 kHz with a little resonance and filter saturation.

Put a frequency shifter on the hat group (example: down 898 Hz), and on other groups as needed. Shifting up gives brighter chill percussion, shifting down gives darker lo-fi. EQ before and after, and re-tune individual elements if one goes weird.
Vocoder on the mid-range rim group: use the self-carrier mode (left as carrier, right as modulator) and enable its chorus.
Put an auto-pan and phaser at a fast unsynced rate (about 6.1 Hz) on the Foley layer, so each pass of the loop lands differently.
Put a volume LFO ducking on half notes over the whole hat/Foley group.

Lo-fi: put a 12-bit sampler at a 22.5 kHz sample rate on the hat group. On the drum bus, run a 12-bit/44.1 kHz stage into a hard clipper (about 2 dB drive) and a symmetric soft saturator (about 1.7 dB). Keep it subtle.

verification: Accent hats are visibly off-grid by varying amounts, not uniform swing.
The kick is low-passed near 1 kHz and the rim focused near 1.5 kHz.
No identical Foley sample repeats on consecutive hits.
Bus drive stays at 2 dB or less.
